# Changelog entries

This page is for developers who release a new version of a site package. A changelog tells an administrator, before
installing, what a release changes. A site package has two: the `<changelog>` inside its `package.xml`, which
travels with the archive and shows on the package page, and the commit history of its source repository. This page
covers both. **Neither is enforced**: a package without a changelog imports and installs. Both are conventions
reviewers expect.

## The changelog element

`eZPackage::parseDOMTree()` reads each `<entry>` of the first `<changelog>`, and each `<change>` inside it:

```xml
<changelog>
  <entry timestamp="1791331200" person="Example Maintainer" email="maintainer@example.com" release="2">
    <change>Updated: the installer activates ezownerchange.</change>
    <change>Added: a German starter page.</change>
  </entry>
  <entry timestamp="1705211779" person="Example Maintainer" email="maintainer@example.com" release="1">
    <change>Creation of package.</change>
  </entry>
</changelog>
```

| Attribute or element | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `timestamp` | When the entry was written, Unix seconds | Without it the entry has no time of its own |
| `person` | Who wrote it | Shown on the package page |
| `email` | How to reach them | Shown as a `mailto:` link on the package page; use an address meant to be public |
| `release` | The `<version><release>` it belongs to | Read and written, not shown |
| `<change>` | One change | One element per change; the page lists each one |

## What writes an entry

| Tool | What it writes |
|---|---|
| The package creation wizard, "Changelog" step (`kernel/classes/ezpackagecreationhandler.php`) | Requires a name, an e-mail and some text, and refuses the step without them. The text starts as `- Creation of package.`; every line starting with `-` or `*` becomes a `<change>`, other lines continue the previous one. The release defaults to the package's release number, or `1` |
| `php ezpm.php create` | One entry, "Creation of package", by the user ezpm runs as |
| A hand-edited `package.xml` | Whatever you write; nothing fills in a missing timestamp |

The wizard's rules are the reason a `<change>` is a single line of text: write one change per element, not a list
inside one element.

## What the package page shows

The package page in the administration (`design/admin4/templates/package/view/full.tpl`) has a Changelog section
when the package has any entries. For each entry it shows the timestamp as a date and time, the person as a link to
the e-mail address, and every `<change>` as a list item. Every value is escaped, so markup in a change shows as
text. The release attribute is not shown, so say in the text which version a change belongs to when it matters.

## What the shipped packages carry

Checked in the two 7x source repositories on 2026-10-18:

- 15 of the 16 packages have exactly one entry, `release="1"`, with the single change "Creation of package.";
  `sevenx_extension` has no changelog.
- Ten entries have a `timestamp` (`1705211779`, 14 January 2024, in the 7x packages; `1791331200`, 7 October 2026,
  in `cjw_multisite_democontent`); the five site packages have none.
- None records the changes made since. Those are in the commit history of the source repositories (see
  [The source repository history](#the-source-repository-history)).

This is the state to improve on, not to copy. A package submitted for publishing should add an entry for every
release it publishes.

## Writing a good entry

- [ ] One `<entry>` per published release, newest first, with `timestamp`, `person` and `release`.
- [ ] One `<change>` per change, starting with `Added:`, `Updated:`, `Removed:` or `Renamed:`, the prefixes the
      7x repositories use for commit subjects.
- [ ] Say what an administrator will notice: a new siteaccess, a changed role, a new extension the installer
      activates, a class attribute added or removed.
- [ ] Name anything that needs action after installing.
- [ ] Use a name and an e-mail address meant to be published. Do not put a private person's address into a public
      package.
- [ ] Keep the old entries. A changelog is history; an entry is never rewritten after its release is published.

> **Note**
> The `<release>` of the entry and the `<version><release>` of the package are the same number. Raise both together
> ([Version numbers](version-numbers.md)).

## The source repository history

The commit history of the source repository is the detailed record. In
[se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage), which holds 1226 commits going back to
2006-10-12, the commit subjects since January 2026 use the prefixes `Updated:` (71), `Fixed:` (29), `Added:` (12)
and `Removed:` (2). A subject names the package and the effect, for example (2026-10-15):

```text
Updated: The multisite installer of the sevenx_multisite package activates ezownerchange, so changing the owner of content is available in a new installation
```

A good release keeps the two in step: the `<change>` lines of the new entry summarise the commits since the last
release. For a changelog file in the repository itself, see
[Keeping a changelog file](../../designers/distribution/keeping-a-changelog-file.md) and
[Changelog prefixes](../../designers/distribution/changelog-prefixes.md).
